pathway.title: EverCommerce Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Revenue durability is average: the base is broad and mostly recurring, but customers can leave quickly. About 93% of customers each contributed less than USD 2 thousand of revenue in fiscal 2025 and about 96% of revenue was recurring or re-occurring, so no single customer failure moves cash flow, yet most contracts are open-ended and can be ended on 30 days' notice. Annualized net revenue retention slipped to about 94% in the second quarter of 2026 from about 97% a year earlier, so the installed base is shrinking before new sales and price increases, and growth now depends on selling more and charging more. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 120; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Margins hold at the gross line but erode below it. Gross margin before depreciation and amortization was 78.23% in the first half of 2026 against 77.75% a year earlier, yet sales and marketing together with product development grew 10.67% against revenue growth of 3.17%, and Adjusted EBITDA fell 5.22% to USD 85.21 million. Reported EBITDA is 20.66% of last-twelve-month revenue and Adjusted EBITDA 29.40%; the gap is USD 52.28 million of add-backs, 29.73% of the adjusted figure, so the adjusted ratios flatter the cushion. Basis: calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Cash flow covers mandatory debt service many times but not shareholder returns on top of it. Free cash flow after cash interest, taxes and capital spending was USD 71.69 million over the last twelve months against scheduled amortization of USD 5.50 million, which is 13.03x cover, but cash share repurchases of USD 82.11 million exceeded free cash flow after amortization by USD 15.92 million and were 3.32x the stock compensation expense. Only USD 19.2 million of the authorization remains, though the board has raised it five times, so the buyback is a discretionary draw on liquidity that the board, under sponsor control, can renew. Basis: calculation C05; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 160; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 54; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Leverage is moderate but not falling, and the term loan is one long bullet. Reported leverage was 4.22x at June 30, 2026 against 4.14x at the end of 2025 and 4.94x at the end of 2024, because last-twelve-month EBITDA slipped while debt fell by only USD 2.45 million in the half. About 95.28% of the principal falls due in July 2031, so repayment rests on refinancing a business whose growth is slowing, helped by lenders having agreed three amendments in 2024 and 2025 that cut margins and pushed maturities out. Basis: calculation C01; calculation C06; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 18–21; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 186–187

Liquidity is adequate and refinancing is a 2030 to 2031 question, not a near-term one. Cash of USD 133.50 million plus the undrawn revolver gives USD 258.50 million after USD 30.0 million of commitments expired on July 6, 2026, before any letters of credit, which the filings cap at a USD 20.0 million sub-limit. The only financial test described is a first lien leverage ratio of 7.50x on the revolver, applied only if more than 35% is drawn, so the filings describe no financial maintenance test for the term loan. Basis: calculation C06; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 51–52; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 54; Source readiness (CP-0); Financial foundation (CP-1)

Interest-rate protection is partial and temporary. Swaps fix the floating rate on USD 425.0 million, 81.1% of the principal, only until October 31, 2027; each 100 bp rise costs about USD 1.0 million a year now and about USD 5.16 million a year once the swaps expire, which would lower reported cash interest cover from 3.73x to 3.23x on last-twelve-month figures. Basis: calculation C07; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 156

Full-year guidance looks back-end loaded, which questions management's forecasting more than the debt. Management said in May that it expected growth to accelerate in the second half and in August that its outlook had moderated, yet the March ranges were unchanged: Adjusted EBITDA of USD 183.0 million to USD 191.0 million and revenue of USD 612.0 million to USD 632.0 million, with results now expected toward the lower end. After USD 85.21 million in the first half and a third-quarter range of USD 44.0 million to USD 46.0 million, the low end needs a fourth quarter of at least USD 51.79 million, 17.29% above the fourth quarter of 2025; two quarters at the third-quarter midpoint would give USD 175.21 million, USD 7.79 million short. Basis: calculation C02; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_evcmq226earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; EX-99.1_2026-03-12_evcm4q25earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-03-12_evcm4q25earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 12; EX-99.1_2026-05-07_evcmq126earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-05-07_evcmq126earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2

Governance is the weakest dimension, and the weakness is about information and control rather than documented creditor harm. Two sponsors hold about 85.7% of the shares and must consent to a change of control, to deals above USD 500.0 million and to chief executive changes while together at 30% or more; the revenue-accounting control weakness has been reported in three annual reports and disclosure controls were not effective at June 30, 2026; and the latest release refers to a new chief executive without detail. No dividend has ever been paid and no sponsor extraction is documented, but the credit agreement that would show what the sponsors may do with cash was not supplied. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 95–98; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 204–206; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 56; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_evcmq226earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A)

runs.text: Dispersed, mostly recurring revenue is the first strength. About 93% of customers each contributed under USD 2 thousand in fiscal 2025 and about 96% of revenue was recurring or re-occurring, so a customer loss is small and renewals repeat; the consequence for creditors is steadier cash flow at moderate leverage, tempered by the issuer's unsized warning of key customers. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 120

A stable gross margin and some pricing power are the second strength. Gross margin was 78.23% in the first half of 2026 and business management revenue rose USD 9.5 million mainly on higher revenue per customer, so price and mix are offsetting weaker retention for now; if retention keeps slipping, price increases become the main lever and carry churn risk. Basis: calculation C03; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 45

A simple, long-dated capital structure is the third strength. One term loan with scheduled amortization of USD 5.50 million a year and an undrawn revolver to July 2030 leave no maturity wall before 2030, so refinancing depends on earnings in 2029 and 2030, not on the next two years. Basis: calculation C06; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 18–21

Free cash flow that covers mandatory debt service is the fourth strength. Free cash flow after cash interest was USD 71.69 million over the last twelve months, 13.03x scheduled amortization, and capital spending including capitalized software was 5.41% of fiscal 2025 revenue, so cash generation does not depend on heavy reinvestment. Basis: calculation C05; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 160

Liquidity with no revolver draw is the fifth strength. Cash of USD 133.50 million and USD 125.0 million of undrawn revolver commitments give USD 258.50 million, and customer deposits and deferred revenue of USD 35.15 million are a non-debt source of funding that would shrink if billings fell; the revolver commitment expired in part on July 6, 2026 and is shown after that date. Basis: calculation C06; calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 20

Governance and reporting reliability are the first weakness. An unremediated revenue-accounting control weakness in three annual reports, controls that were not effective at June 30, 2026 and an unexplained chief executive transition reduce confidence in the figures creditors rely on and in management continuity, while sponsor consent rights let two holders steer capital policy. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 204–206; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 56; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_evcmq226earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 95–98

Earnings quality is the second weakness. Add-backs of USD 52.28 million are 29.73% of Adjusted EBITDA and include stock compensation of USD 24.75 million and transaction costs that have appeared every year, so reported leverage of 4.22x is the safer anchor and the 2.96x adjusted figure an upper bound on the cushion. Basis: calculation C01; calculation C03; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Slipping retention and rising spending are the third weakness. Retention of about 94% and spending growth of 10.67% against revenue growth of 3.17% mean EBITDA is falling before any economic shock, leaving less room to absorb one. Basis: calculation C03; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46

Shareholder returns above free cash flow are the fourth weakness. Repurchases of USD 82.11 million over the last twelve months exceed free cash flow after amortization by USD 15.92 million, and the board, under sponsor control, can renew the authorization, so cash that could repay debt returns to equity instead. Basis: calculation C05; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 54; Business & governance (CP-1A)

A bullet maturity with a floating rate is the fifth weakness. 95.28% of principal is due in July 2031 and the swaps that fix 81.1% of the loan end in October 2027, so both repayment and interest cost depend on conditions in 2027 to 2031 that no document fixes. Basis: calculation C06; calculation C07; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 18–21

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: No new debt was issued in the period read. The company repriced and extended its term loan and revolver three times: an amendment on December 13, 2024 cut the margin and removed the credit spread adjustment; one on June 10, 2025 reduced the revolver to USD 155.0 million and extended USD 125.0 million of it; and one on July 29, 2025 pushed the term loan maturity to July 6, 2031 and the extended revolver to July 29, 2030. For creditors this removed any maturity before 2030 and lowered cash interest, and it shows lenders were willing to extend. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 186–187; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20

The company completed one acquisition and two disposals. ZyraTalk, an AI customer-engagement business, was bought on September 15, 2025 for about USD 36.0 million in cash, with up to USD 6.5 million of contingent consideration over three years. The marketing technology solutions business was sold on October 31, 2025 for about USD 45.0 million in cash and fitness solutions were sold in 2024. The disposals shrink revenue and are presented as discontinued operations, so fiscal and quarterly comparisons exclude them. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10

fields.value: Financial foundation for EverCommerce Inc. as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is consolidated continuing-operations statements for fiscal 2023 to 2025 and the half and quarters to June 30, 2026, reported and issuer-adjusted EBITDA, cash interest paid, debt at carrying value, liquidity and events after the balance-sheet date.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EverCommerce's single secured term loan is serviceable but less lightly levered than the issuer's adjusted figures suggest: gross debt is 4.22x last-twelve-month reported EBITDA at June 30, 2026, against 2.96x on the adjusted measure, and the balloon is not due until 2031.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt is 3.14x reported EBITDA and reported EBITDA covers cash interest 3.73x, so servicing is comfortable on cash figures the issuer itself reports. The adjusted ratios rest on USD 52.28 million of add-backs, mostly stock compensation and one-off costs, and adjusted EBITDA has slipped below the fiscal 2025 level as management guides to the low end of its range. The main contrary point is an undrawn revolver and no balloon before 2031, which limits refinancing pressure. The view would worsen if adjusted EBITDA keeps falling or if buybacks again exceed free cash flow.

fields.value: Leverage is moderate and its direction is flat to slightly worse. Gross debt at carrying value fell by only USD 2.449 million between December 31, 2025 and June 30, 2026 while last-twelve-month reported EBITDA fell below the fiscal 2025 figure, because sales and marketing and product development spending rose by more than the whole increase in revenue in the first half of 2026. For creditors this means deleveraging is coming from debt paydown that is too small to matter, not from earnings growth, so the reported ratio has edged up from 4.14x to 4.22x even though the issuer's adjusted ratio looks lower.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The gap between reported and adjusted EBITDA is entirely three issuer add-backs. Stock-based compensation recurs in every period and is a real economic cost, because the company issues shares to staff and spends cash on repurchases, which adjusted EBITDA ignores. The transaction-related and other non-recurring line has been present in every year shown, which means its non-recurring character is not established, and the issuer gives no component split. A creditor should therefore anchor on the reported ratio and treat the adjusted ratio as an upper bound on earnings quality, not as a covenant calculation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest offset is cash generation and a small, simple capital structure. Free cash flow after cash interest and capital spending was positive in every period shown, and a single term loan with scheduled amortization of USD 5.500 million a year leaves no refinancing event before the 2031 balloon. The offset is weakened by capital allocation: fiscal 2025 repurchases exceeded free cash flow, and cash fell even with disposal proceeds. First-half 2026 repurchases were covered by free cash flow, so the observable test is whether that holds as earnings soften. Cash flow figures are consolidated and still include the sold marketing business, so they overstate continuing cash generation to an extent the filings do not quantify.

fields.value: Liquidity is adequate and not the near-term constraint. Cash at June 30, 2026 plus the undrawn revolver, before letters of credit, is the only liquidity the filings establish; USD 30.0 million of the commitments expired on July 6, 2026, a dated later event that is not blended into the period figure. The revolver carries a springing first lien leverage test that applies only if more than 35% of commitments are drawn, nothing is drawn, and the reported ratio is not stated, so covenant headroom cannot be calculated from these tables. Interest rate protection is a second watch item: swaps cover most of the term loan only until October 31, 2027, after which the whole loan floats, while the issuer's own sensitivity today is small.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customer deposits and deferred revenue are a non-debt funding source and not ordinary payables. Together they stand at about USD 35.152 million and have grown slowly from December 2024, so customers prepay for services the company must still deliver. A drop in billings would remove this float before revenue falls, which makes these two lines an early indicator to monitor alongside net revenue retention.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A supported downside sequence starts with weaker retention: the annualized net revenue retention rate was about 94% in the second quarter of 2026 against about 97% a year earlier, and pro forma revenue growth in that quarter was 2.0%. Slower growth against rising sales and product spending would first compress EBITDA, which raises leverage on a debt balance that barely amortizes; cash and the undrawn revolver would then absorb any shortfall, with repurchases the discretionary outflow. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and governance review of EverCommerce Inc. as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the business, ownership, sponsor and governance facts, transactions and capital allocation that matter to a creditor, from the annual report, three quarterly reports and three earnings releases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No external sources were used. The run settings are not an issuer source and are not listed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EverCommerce is a diversified, mostly recurring small-business software company whose main credit risk is control rather than customers: two sponsors hold about 85.7% of the stock with consent rights over key decisions, while growth is slowing and spending is outrunning revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No sponsor action adverse to creditors is documented: the company has never paid a dividend, its refinancings extended maturities and cut margins, and the latest acquisition was paid in cash. Against that, the issuer reports an unremediated revenue-accounting control weakness and refers to a new chief executive without saying who, when or on what terms, so management continuity is a question, not a finding.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 186–187; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 204–206; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_evcmq226earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is broad and mostly recurring, so near-term cash flow does not depend on a few customers. About 93% of customers each contributed less than USD 2 thousand of revenue in fiscal 2025, and about 96% of revenue was recurring or re-occurring. The mechanism is dispersion across a large base, which supports debt service at a moderate leverage level. The issuer also warns of key customers and a more pronounced concentration in certain markets without sizing them, so dispersion is established by customer count, not by revenue share.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 120; calculation C01

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Growth is modest and retention is slipping, which is the main operating threat to coverage. Revenue grew 3.2% in the first half of 2026 against 4.8% in fiscal 2025, and annualized net revenue retention was about 94% in the second quarter against about 97% a year earlier. A customer base that sheds revenue faster than it adds it forces more sales spending just to hold earnings steady.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Spending is growing faster than revenue, so the earnings cushion is thinning. In the first half of 2026 sales and marketing rose 12.5% and product development 7.9%, together more than the whole revenue increase, and Adjusted EBITDA fell to USD 85.21 million from USD 89.90 million. If revenue growth does not recover, the same spending base erodes cash interest cover before it threatens liquidity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The acquisition programme has slowed and the latest purchase is dilutive in the near term. The company has acquired 54 companies since inception, paid about USD 36.0 million in cash for ZyraTalk in September 2025 with up to USD 6.5 million more contingent over three years, and added no debt to do so. In the first half of 2026 ZyraTalk contributed USD 1.8 million of revenue against USD 5.3 million of post-acquisition operating expense, so it adds to the earnings drag until it scales.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 185; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 45–47; calculation C06

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Control sits with two sponsors whose consent rights reach the decisions creditors care about, but no creditor-adverse use of them is documented. While the sponsors together hold at least 30% of the stock they must consent to a change of control, to any acquisition or disposal above USD 500.0 million, to hiring or removing the chief executive and to insolvency filings, and each can nominate directors while it holds at least 5%. This gives them the discretion to change capital policy without creditor consent unless the credit agreement, which is not supplied, restrains it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reporting quality is the weakest part of governance. The issuer has disclosed the same revenue-accounting control weakness in its fiscal 2023, 2024 and 2025 annual reports and its disclosure controls were not effective at June 30, 2026. The statements still carry a clean audit opinion, so the risk is that revenue, receivables and deferred revenue are less reliable than their precision suggests.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is the sponsors' conduct on the record: no dividend has ever been paid, the only shareholder payments are cash-funded share repurchases, and the 2024 and 2025 amendments pushed the term loan to July 2031 and lowered its margin. A business with hundreds of thousands of customers and recurring revenue can absorb slower growth without a funding event.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A second counterpoint to the diversification finding is the issuer's own warning of key customers and more concentration in certain markets, which the filings do not size; a disclosed share above a tenth of revenue would weaken that finding. The view would improve if the control weakness is reported remediated, if retention and growth recover, and if the proxy statement and credit agreement show no related-party fees or distribution capacity beyond what the filings describe. It would worsen if the chief executive change proves disorderly, if the sponsors sell down or the board approves a debt-funded payment to shareholders, or if buybacks again exceed the cash the business generates.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement that holds related-party transactions, sponsor fees, executive pay and each sponsor's individual percentage was not supplied, so the finding that no creditor-adverse sponsor action is documented covers only the annual and quarterly filings and releases read.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Revenue by vertical, the size of the key customers the issuer warns about and any investor presentation were not supplied, so the diversification finding rests on customer counts and revenue type, not on business-line or customer shares.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The only reference to a chief executive transition is one sentence in the latest release, so the management-continuity point is an open question and no view is taken on who leads or when.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The credit agreement that limits dividends, investments and asset sales was not supplied, so what the sponsors may do with cash, as opposed to what they have done, is not assessed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No new debt was issued in the period read. The company repriced and extended its term loan and revolver three times: an amendment on December 13, 2024 cut the margin and removed the credit spread adjustment; one on June 10, 2025 reduced the revolver to USD 155.0 million and extended USD 125.0 million of it; and one on July 29, 2025 pushed the term loan maturity to July 6, 2031 and the extended revolver to July 29, 2030. For creditors this removed any maturity before 2030 and lowered cash interest, and it shows lenders were willing to extend.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The company completed one acquisition and two disposals. ZyraTalk, an AI customer-engagement business, was bought on September 15, 2025 for about USD 36.0 million in cash, with up to USD 6.5 million of contingent consideration over three years. The marketing technology solutions business was sold on October 31, 2025 for about USD 45.0 million in cash and fitness solutions were sold in 2024. The disposals shrink revenue and are presented as discontinued operations, so fiscal and quarterly comparisons exclude them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The level is driven by concentrated sponsor control with consent rights, because that lets two holders steer capital policy and management change without creditor consent, which implies a raised monitoring posture rather than a documented loss of protection. Countervailing evidence is that no dividend, recapitalization or other creditor-adverse action is documented and that lenders extended maturities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit assessment of EverCommerce Inc. as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the integrated credit view built on the annual report, three quarterly reports and three earnings releases and on the accepted source readiness, financial foundation and business and governance analyses. It gives no rating, legal-capacity conclusion, recovery value or portfolio sizing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No external sources were used. The run settings are not an issuer source and are not listed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EverCommerce is an adequate credit, not a strong one: recurring, widely spread revenue and a single term loan not due until 2031 support debt service, while slowing growth, add-back-heavy earnings and sponsor control leave little room for error. Gross debt is 4.22x reported EBITDA and 2.96x the issuer's adjusted measure, and reported EBITDA covers cash interest 3.73x, so servicing is comfortable today.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main downside path is weaker customer retention and spending that grows faster than revenue eroding earnings while share repurchases continue. Full-year guidance also needs a fourth quarter the company has not yet reported, which tests management's forecasting more than debt service.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue durability is average: the base is broad and mostly recurring, but customers can leave quickly. About 93% of customers each contributed less than USD 2 thousand of revenue in fiscal 2025 and about 96% of revenue was recurring or re-occurring, so no single customer failure moves cash flow, yet most contracts are open-ended and can be ended on 30 days' notice. Annualized net revenue retention slipped to about 94% in the second quarter of 2026 from about 97% a year earlier, so the installed base is shrinking before new sales and price increases, and growth now depends on selling more and charging more.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 120; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins hold at the gross line but erode below it. Gross margin before depreciation and amortization was 78.23% in the first half of 2026 against 77.75% a year earlier, yet sales and marketing together with product development grew 10.67% against revenue growth of 3.17%, and Adjusted EBITDA fell 5.22% to USD 85.21 million. Reported EBITDA is 20.66% of last-twelve-month revenue and Adjusted EBITDA 29.40%; the gap is USD 52.28 million of add-backs, 29.73% of the adjusted figure, so the adjusted ratios flatter the cushion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash flow covers mandatory debt service many times but not shareholder returns on top of it. Free cash flow after cash interest, taxes and capital spending was USD 71.69 million over the last twelve months against scheduled amortization of USD 5.50 million, which is 13.03x cover, but cash share repurchases of USD 82.11 million exceeded free cash flow after amortization by USD 15.92 million and were 3.32x the stock compensation expense. Only USD 19.2 million of the authorization remains, though the board has raised it five times, so the buyback is a discretionary draw on liquidity that the board, under sponsor control, can renew.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C05; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 160; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 54; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is moderate but not falling, and the term loan is one long bullet. Reported leverage was 4.22x at June 30, 2026 against 4.14x at the end of 2025 and 4.94x at the end of 2024, because last-twelve-month EBITDA slipped while debt fell by only USD 2.45 million in the half. About 95.28% of the principal falls due in July 2031, so repayment rests on refinancing a business whose growth is slowing, helped by lenders having agreed three amendments in 2024 and 2025 that cut margins and pushed maturities out.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C01; calculation C06; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 18–21; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 186–187

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate and refinancing is a 2030 to 2031 question, not a near-term one. Cash of USD 133.50 million plus the undrawn revolver gives USD 258.50 million after USD 30.0 million of commitments expired on July 6, 2026, before any letters of credit, which the filings cap at a USD 20.0 million sub-limit. The only financial test described is a first lien leverage ratio of 7.50x on the revolver, applied only if more than 35% is drawn, so the filings describe no financial maintenance test for the term loan.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest-rate protection is partial and temporary. Swaps fix the floating rate on USD 425.0 million, 81.1% of the principal, only until October 31, 2027; each 100 bp rise costs about USD 1.0 million a year now and about USD 5.16 million a year once the swaps expire, which would lower reported cash interest cover from 3.73x to 3.23x on last-twelve-month figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Full-year guidance looks back-end loaded, which questions management's forecasting more than the debt. Management said in May that it expected growth to accelerate in the second half and in August that its outlook had moderated, yet the March ranges were unchanged: Adjusted EBITDA of USD 183.0 million to USD 191.0 million and revenue of USD 612.0 million to USD 632.0 million, with results now expected toward the lower end. After USD 85.21 million in the first half and a third-quarter range of USD 44.0 million to USD 46.0 million, the low end needs a fourth quarter of at least USD 51.79 million, 17.29% above the fourth quarter of 2025; two quarters at the third-quarter midpoint would give USD 175.21 million, USD 7.79 million short.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C02; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_evcmq226earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; EX-99.1_2026-03-12_evcm4q25earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-03-12_evcm4q25earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 12; EX-99.1_2026-05-07_evcmq126earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-05-07_evcmq126earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance is the weakest dimension, and the weakness is about information and control rather than documented creditor harm. Two sponsors hold about 85.7% of the shares and must consent to a change of control, to deals above USD 500.0 million and to chief executive changes while together at 30% or more; the revenue-accounting control weakness has been reported in three annual reports and disclosure controls were not effective at June 30, 2026; and the latest release refers to a new chief executive without detail. No dividend has ever been paid and no sponsor extraction is documented, but the credit agreement that would show what the sponsors may do with cash was not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 95–98; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 204–206; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 56; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_evcmq226earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is conduct and cash. The 2026 quarterly ranges were met or beaten: first-quarter Adjusted EBITDA of USD 40.67 million sat inside a range of USD 39.0 million to USD 41.0 million and second-quarter USD 44.54 million was above a range of USD 41.0 million to USD 43.0 million. First-half repurchases of USD 28.57 million were covered by free cash flow of USD 36.08 million, free cash flow has been positive in every period reported, no dividend has ever been paid, and adjusted leverage of 2.96x leaves room for earnings to fall before servicing is stressed. Lenders also agreed three amendments that lowered margins and extended maturities, which shows market access.

fields.value: This view would win if retention stabilizes near 97%, discretionary spending growth fades toward revenue growth so that EBITDA stops falling, and the fourth quarter delivers the step-up the guidance requires; the credit would then rate better than adequate. It would worsen if third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA falls below USD 44.0 million, if the revolver is drawn, if the repurchase authorization is raised again while repurchases exceed free cash flow, if the sponsors sell below 30% or the chief executive change proves disorderly, or if the control weakness is still unremediated in the next annual report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No creditor-protection document was supplied, so the conclusion that servicing is comfortable rests on cash flow and not on contractual rights: what the term lenders can enforce, how much the sponsors may distribute and how large any letters of credit are remain unknown, the covenant's own ratio and EBITDA definition are not stated so the leverage ratios here are not covenant calculations, and the liquidity figure stays gross of letters of credit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No peer or sector benchmark was supplied, so "adequate" and "moderate" compare the issuer with its own history and with the 7.50x revolver test, not with other leveraged software issuers, and the business profile against typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The back-end loading finding is the analyst's arithmetic on the issuer's published ranges; the issuer gives no quantified bridge to the fourth quarter beyond a May statement that growth should accelerate, so an unannounced price increase, acquisition or timing item could make the ranges reachable and the finding would then fall away.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The filings do not split revenue growth between price and volume or give retention by customer group beyond one rate, so how much of the weaker retention is controllable cannot be established and the cost-flexibility estimate carries that uncertainty.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Dispersed, mostly recurring revenue is the first strength. About 93% of customers each contributed under USD 2 thousand in fiscal 2025 and about 96% of revenue was recurring or re-occurring, so a customer loss is small and renewals repeat; the consequence for creditors is steadier cash flow at moderate leverage, tempered by the issuer's unsized warning of key customers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A stable gross margin and some pricing power are the second strength. Gross margin was 78.23% in the first half of 2026 and business management revenue rose USD 9.5 million mainly on higher revenue per customer, so price and mix are offsetting weaker retention for now; if retention keeps slipping, price increases become the main lever and carry churn risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A simple, long-dated capital structure is the third strength. One term loan with scheduled amortization of USD 5.50 million a year and an undrawn revolver to July 2030 leave no maturity wall before 2030, so refinancing depends on earnings in 2029 and 2030, not on the next two years.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow that covers mandatory debt service is the fourth strength. Free cash flow after cash interest was USD 71.69 million over the last twelve months, 13.03x scheduled amortization, and capital spending including capitalized software was 5.41% of fiscal 2025 revenue, so cash generation does not depend on heavy reinvestment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity with no revolver draw is the fifth strength. Cash of USD 133.50 million and USD 125.0 million of undrawn revolver commitments give USD 258.50 million, and customer deposits and deferred revenue of USD 35.15 million are a non-debt source of funding that would shrink if billings fell; the revolver commitment expired in part on July 6, 2026 and is shown after that date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C06; calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance and reporting reliability are the first weakness. An unremediated revenue-accounting control weakness in three annual reports, controls that were not effective at June 30, 2026 and an unexplained chief executive transition reduce confidence in the figures creditors rely on and in management continuity, while sponsor consent rights let two holders steer capital policy.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings quality is the second weakness. Add-backs of USD 52.28 million are 29.73% of Adjusted EBITDA and include stock compensation of USD 24.75 million and transaction costs that have appeared every year, so reported leverage of 4.22x is the safer anchor and the 2.96x adjusted figure an upper bound on the cushion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C01; calculation C03; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Slipping retention and rising spending are the third weakness. Retention of about 94% and spending growth of 10.67% against revenue growth of 3.17% mean EBITDA is falling before any economic shock, leaving less room to absorb one.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns above free cash flow are the fourth weakness. Repurchases of USD 82.11 million over the last twelve months exceed free cash flow after amortization by USD 15.92 million, and the board, under sponsor control, can renew the authorization, so cash that could repay debt returns to equity instead.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C05; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 54; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A bullet maturity with a floating rate is the fifth weakness. 95.28% of principal is due in July 2031 and the swaps that fix 81.1% of the loan end in October 2027, so both repayment and interest cost depend on conditions in 2027 to 2031 that no document fixes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C06; calculation C07; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 18–21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The nine-dimension view is as follows. Scale and market position is average: last-twelve-month revenue of USD 598.10 million in fragmented markets with low barriers to entry. Competitive advantage is average: integrated vertical workflows raise switching costs, but most contracts end on 30 days' notice and retention is slipping. Business diversification is strong: customers are dispersed across home, health and wellness services and 88.79% of first-half 2026 revenue is from the United States, which limits currency exposure. Cost and capex flexibility is average: sales, marketing and product development are 36.53% of first-half revenue and can be slowed, but rent, salaries and debt service are fixed or semi-fixed. Margin stability is average: gross margin is steady and the EBITDA margin is falling. Free cash flow stability is average: positive in every period but on a perimeter that still includes the sold business. Ability to refinance is average: three amendments show access, but 95.28% of the principal is one 2031 bullet in a sponsor-controlled company. Liquidity is strong on stated figures at USD 258.50 million against USD 33.11 million of last-twelve-month cash interest, before letters of credit. Financial policy and governance is weak: concentrated control, a persistent control weakness and buybacks above free cash flow after amortization, offset by no dividend ever paid.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C04; calculation C06; calculation C08; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 33–35; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 58; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EverCommerce sells vertically tailored software to service small and medium businesses in home, health and wellness services, bundling business management, billing and payments and customer-experience tools in one segment. Revenue visibility comes from subscription and transaction fees, 96.27% of fiscal 2025 revenue, and the cash-generation mechanism is simple: recurring fees on a dispersed base funded from a low-capital-intensity model. Ownership is concentrated in two sponsors that hold about 85.7% of the shares, so the credit depends on their financial policy rather than on public-market discipline; the filings name no parent, and the creditors' claim sits on the operating group through subsidiary guarantees and pledged equity under the credit facilities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9–11; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 95; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 51; calculation C08; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The roll-up history matters for creditors only through cash and earnings. The company has bought 54 businesses since inception, paid about USD 36.0 million in cash for ZyraTalk in September 2025 with no new debt, and sold its marketing technology business for about USD 45.0 million in cash in October 2025, so acquisitions are now funded from cash and the disposal shrank revenue; ZyraTalk added USD 1.8 million of first-half revenue against USD 5.3 million of operating expense, an early drag on EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 45–47; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is predictable and recurring but not contractually locked. Business management software drove a USD 9.5 million rise in first-half subscription and transaction revenue, mainly through higher revenue per customer, billing and payment solutions added USD 0.8 million on volume and a slightly higher take rate, and rebates from group purchasing fell USD 1.4 million. Payments are about 20% of revenue and depend on card networks and processors, so a pricing-led increase combined with falling retention makes revenue more sensitive to churn and to small-business spending than the recurring label suggests.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins can be defended against volume pressure only if discretionary spending is slowed. Cost of revenues is steady, but sales and marketing rose 12.49% and product development 7.94% in the first half, and the increase over the prior-year spending ratio is worth about USD 7.42 million per half-year, or 8.44% of last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA when annualized. That is a real management lever, but pulling it trades near-term EBITDA for slower growth in a business where retention is already weakening.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion is good before shareholder returns. Free cash flow before cash interest was 84.82% of last-twelve-month reported EBITDA and 59.60% of Adjusted EBITDA; the gap to the adjusted figure reflects capital spending, taxes and the transaction-related costs that the issuer adds back but pays in cash, which makes the adjusted measure a poor guide to cash. The weakness is the use of that cash, since capitalized software has risen faster than expense and buybacks absorb more than the cash left after amortization.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The claims outside the debt figure are small against cash generation. Operating lease liabilities of USD 12.01 million, USD 13.24 million undiscounted with a weighted remaining term of 3.89 years, sit outside debt and their cost is already inside EBITDA; non-cancelable purchase obligations for software services, mail, fulfilment and hosting total USD 31.97 million to 2029; and up to USD 6.5 million of ZyraTalk contingent consideration may be paid over three years. Together the leases and purchase obligations are USD 43.98 million, less than one year of free cash flow. The company has no finance leases and the sources read show no pensions, retiree medical, factoring or supply-chain finance, and the Delaware class action carries no accrual because a loss is not probable or estimable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry is high and caps pricing. The issuer competes with manual processes, vertical specialists and horizontal vendors including Salesforce, Intuit and Square, and describes barriers to entry as generally low, so spending to defend retention is structural and margin gains are hard to hold. New entrants and substitutes work through the same mechanism: the filings expect more entrants and name partners that may become competitors, and the analyst view is that AI-native tools are a further substitute the filings do not size, so each raises the sales and product spending needed to keep revenue per customer rising. Buyer power is individually weak but collectively strong, because small customers can leave on 30 days' notice and are price-sensitive in a downturn. Supplier power is moderate: card networks and payment processors sit between the company and about 20% of its revenue and can fine or terminate it for non-compliance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Economic and regulatory factors are material to credit; currency and politics are not. A weaker economy could close small businesses at higher rates, shrink card volumes and slow spending on software, and the company says fixed and semi-fixed costs including debt service cannot be cut quickly; interest-rate rises matter through the floating-rate term loan. Payment-network rules, data-privacy law and AI regulation raise compliance cost but are not quantified in the filings, and international revenue is 11.21% of the first half, so currency is minor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 24–25; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; calculation C08

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit-translated SWOT is as follows. Strengths are dispersed recurring revenue, a stable gross margin, a long simple capital structure and positive free cash flow. Weaknesses are slipping retention, add-back-heavy earnings, a persistent control weakness and repurchases above free cash flow after amortization. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are payments cross-selling and AI products raising revenue per customer, remediation of the control weakness and holding repurchases inside free cash flow. Threats that could weaken it are a small-business downturn, price competition from low-barrier entrants, rising rates after the swaps expire and a sponsor sell-down or disorderly chief executive change.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 54; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_evcmq226earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C05; calculation C07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over 12 to 24 months the issuer's own guidance and the swap expiry set the picture. Management expects results toward the lower end of ranges that were unchanged since March, quarterly results have so far met or beaten their ranges, and no maturity falls due beyond USD 5.50 million of amortization a year; headwinds are retention near 94%, spending that outruns revenue, the dilutive ZyraTalk purchase and the October 2027 swap expiry. A hearing on the sponsors' chief executive approval right was scheduled for October 19, 2026 and its outcome is not in the sources.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C02; calculation C09; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_evcmq226earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-06-30_evcm-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the question is refinancing. The revolver matures in July 2030 and the term loan in July 2031, so the 2029 and 2030 results decide the terms of a refinancing of about USD 523.88 million of principal; sector tailwinds are small-business demand for vertical software and digital payments, and sector headwinds are small-business failures, competitive entry and consolidation of customers, which can bring fee pressure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C06; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 58

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The realistic downside begins with the customer base, not a lender event. A soft economy closes small businesses and cuts card volumes while retention, already near 94%, slips further and contracts end on 30 days' notice, so revenue growth stalls; because spending is rising 10.67% and rent, salaries and debt service are semi-fixed, EBITDA falls faster than revenue. Each USD 10.0 million of lost last-twelve-month reported EBITDA lifts gross leverage from 4.22x to 4.59x and lowers reported cash interest cover from 3.73x to 3.43x, and the pressure compounds if floating-rate cost rises after October 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C07; calculation C11; 10-K_2025-12-31_evcm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 58

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity would absorb the shock before covenants or maturities matter. With free cash flow of USD 71.69 million and cash of USD 133.50 million, only a revolver draw above 35% of commitments, which is USD 43.75 million, would start the first lien leverage test of 7.50x; with zero operating cash flow, cash alone would meet cash interest and amortization for 3.46 years and cash plus the full revolver, if it stayed available, for 6.70 years. The levers are suspending buybacks of USD 82.11 million a year, slowing spending by about USD 7.42 million per half-year and capitalized software of USD 15.58 million per half-year, and resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress within two years; the exposure is the 2030 to 2031 refinancing if EBITDA is lower by then.

fields.value: Overall, EverCommerce presents an adequate business profile supported by dispersed recurring revenue and a stable gross margin, but credit quality is constrained by slowing growth, add-back-heavy earnings and sponsor-controlled governance with a weak reporting record. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow covers scheduled amortization 13.03x, although it does not cover buybacks on top. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on EBITDA stabilizing before the revolver matures in July 2030 and the term loan in July 2031, and on lenders' continued appetite. The primary downside path is weaker retention and spending that outruns revenue pressing EBITDA and leverage while repurchases continue. The profile against typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector is not established because no peer set was supplied. Further analysis would require the credit agreement, the proxy statement, peer benchmarks and the filings for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. Top risk: retention-led earnings erosion ahead of a 2031 bullet refinancing.
